{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZgQXRg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDHZJc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 49, "title": "Correct V30MZ flags after successful byte IDIV", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `f9464ad5f50dfc5f362fe6c1ea0cf3846394690b`, `crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs:1050–1062` clears only OF after successful byte signed division (`F6 /7`). Other arithmetic flags retain incoming values, conflicting with the inspected WonderSwan CPU experiment. Subsequent conditional branches can therefore take incorrect paths; commercial-title impact remains unmeasured.

Static reproduction, not executed during planning: `F6 FB` with AX=`0006`, BL=`02`, FLAGS=`F002` produces AX=`0003` but retains FLAGS=`F002`; expected FLAGS are `F006`.

## Expected outcome

Successful byte IDIV clears AF, CF and OF; derives SF from quotient AL bit 7, ZF from AL being zero, and PF from even parity of AL. Preserve unrelated FLAGS bits, quotient AL, remainder AH, operand sampling, instruction continuation and existing accounting.

Apply this behavior to emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations, independently of graphics mode.

## Context

The clean checkout and inspected remote main match the baseline. The open Issue/PR collection is empty; inspection of 48 closed entries found no equivalent completed task. [Issue #47](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/47) and [PR #48](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/pull/48) explicitly preserved byte division while correcting word flags.

The [NEC V30MZ manual](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/lbr/v30mztm-hardware-preliminary), §3.1.5, specifies cleared division overflow and leaves other division flags unspecified. This does not establish preservation. The pinned [WSCPUTest report](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/README.md) supplies the successful byte-IDIV rule. Its [assembly experiment and calculator](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/WSCpuTest.asm#L5287) compare full FLAGS under contrasting inputs and calculate successful SZP from AL. The calculator’s F202 base includes its incoming IF; preserve caller control flags instead of forcing that constant. Register experiments are inspected source evidence, without independently inspected per-model measurement logs; mapped-operand and graphics-mode applicability are instruction-level inferences.

Correction record: replace the unsupported assumption that clearing OF while retaining other arithmetic flags adequately models successful byte IDIV. Record the old assumption, corrected rule, sources and rationale. Evidence-based corrections need no human approval or independent AI re-review; preserve the goal and relevant acceptance.

Scope is this successful instruction path and necessary native/Wasm/browser coverage. Byte DIV multiplication history, signed exceptional results, fault flags/classification, decimal adjustment and absolute timing remain unresolved separate work. The experiment routes quotient magnitude 128 to its exceptional path: use unambiguous successful boundaries ±127 here and preserve existing classification without presenting it as hardware-correct.

Existing full-FLAGS cartridge coverage targets word division. [Saved #47 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/f9464ad5f50dfc5f362fe6c1ea0cf3846394690b/docs/issue-47-validation.md) reports 135 core tests, 21 integration tests, one adapter test and both complete Chromium suites passing. These are Coordinator-reported results, not planning-time reruns.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the successful `F6 /7` flag rule through ordinary decoding. Document the assumption correction and source limits. Preserve word DIV/IDIV, byte DIV and existing fault behavior.
- [ ] Add independent literal AX/full-FLAGS vectors under contrasting incoming arithmetic and TF/IF/DF patterns. Cover zero, positive/negative quotients, all operand-sign combinations, exact/inexact division, parity differences and ±127 successful boundaries. Include nonzero AH with zero AL to prove SZP uses AL: incoming F002, AX=0001, divisor=02 must produce AX=0100 and FLAGS=F046. Also include the reproduction and AX=FFF9/divisor=02 → AX=FFFD, FLAGS=F082. Expectations must not call production flag helpers.
- [ ] Exercise register divisors, successful AL/AH divisor aliases, and mapped RAM/ROM/SRAM byte operands at even and odd addresses with segment overrides. Assert operand sampling before writeback, unchanged source memory and unrelated state, exact continuation, and following Z/C/O/S/P/signed-condition branches. Preserve the existing 24-clock execution component and access charges; verify one normal-machine step advances shared devices once using its returned cost.
- [ ] Cover emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations, supported monochrome/color graphics modes and runtime mode transitions. Record actual pre-fix focused native-test and original cartridge-probe failures, followed by corrected passes. Preserve division faults, word flags, byte DIV, multiplication, shifts, prefixes, interrupts, HALT and DMA regressions.
- [ ] Add or extend an original source-included CC0 fixture using existing tooling. Native and production Chromium/Wasm acceptance must compare actual CPU-written AX, full FLAGS and branch observations on every model and fresh restart. Clear volatile observations, invalidate retained completion and use fresh execution markers so poisoned stale saves cannot satisfy acceptance. Retain existing word-division assertions.
- [ ] Before merge, the Coordinator runs `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `git diff --check`. In `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against the production preview. Preserve three-model gates, firmware-free startup, video/input/frame continuity, audio/PCM, GDMA/SDMA/Hyper Voice, SRAM/EEPROM and browser save integrity.
- [ ] Update `docs/hardware-subset.md` and relevant source/provenance documentation. Record actual commands, failures, resolutions, passes and unperformed checks. The Coordinator reviews the final diff against every checkbox before merge, retaining prior acceptance and distinguishing bounded emulator evidence from commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

Baseline production-Chromium discrimination, additional browser engines and additional lawfully available software. Physical-console comparisons and human gameplay are optional observations. None were performed during planning; none blocks merge or requires confirmation.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.

This autonomous campaign has no human-approval gate. Mandatory acceptance uses
automated native and production-browser tests on the emulator's supported model
and mode configurations. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are
optional evidence and must remain explicitly unperformed unless actually available.
Do not invent device identities, real-device results or a requirement for human
confirmation. Resolve technical errors with recorded evidence and automated checks
through the existing Coordinator workflow.
